subject: Re: Intermittent hung generation observed by SkyPort - support ticket #SP-8342
messages:
From: Alan Price <alan@skyportlogistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: SkyPort Engineering <eng@skyportlogistics.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hung generation observed in production - examples included

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing intermittent requests to Redwood API that never returned a completion yesterday afternoon. The requests time out on our side after 30s. We captured a couple of examples where the token stream never resumed. This is affecting a small subset (~0.2%) of user actions — not a full outage but enough for us to open a ticket.

Attached are a short error snippet and the request/response headers from one affected session. Example behavior: request is accepted (200), then no additional tokens arrive for >30s, client eventually gives up. We retried the same prompt and it completed normally, so it looks non-deterministic.

Can you confirm whether Redwood observed any platform-side stalls or queued requests that would explain this? Ticket: SP-8342.

Thanks,
Alan Price
Senior Product Manager
SkyPort Logistics

Attachments: error_snippet.txt (text), session_headers.json (json)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-06-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hung generation observed in production - examples included

Hi Alan — thanks for the quick report and the files. We opened internal ticket RI-6129 and started a triage.

Quick notes / asks from our side:
- Can you paste the exact request IDs (X-Request-ID / x-redwood-req) from the session_headers.json for the two failed attempts? That will let us look at routing and kernel selection traces.
- Were the affected requests all going to the same model and region (e.g., redwood/gpt-large-us-west-1)?
- You mentioned retries completed normally — do you have timestamps for both the failed and the successful attempts?

We’ll check runtime traces for stalls, GPU throttling, and any transient routing fallbacks. If we don’t see platform-side evidence we’ll share guidance for SDK/keepalive behavior to rule out client-side connection handling.

We’ll update within 24 hours or sooner if we find anything.

—Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alan Price <alan@skyportlogistics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hung generation observed in production - examples included

Hi Alan — thank you for the IDs and timestamps; very helpful. Final triage summary from Redwood (RI-6129):

Summary of findings
- We traced both request IDs through the routing layer and runtime. There were no queuing delays, GPU preemption events, or kernel failures recorded for those requests. Internal logs show normal inference progress and token emit events on our side that align with the successful retry.
- Network telemetry around the time of the failed request shows an unusual TCP retransmission spike originating from the customer ELB IP (see linked traces). That coincides with the gap in tokens your team observed.
- We reviewed model-side health and telemetry for the redwood/llm-3b-us-opt instance pool; no errors, restarts, or capacity constraints were present.

Conclusion
- We were unable to reproduce a Redwood platform-side stall for the reported events. Evidence suggests the interruption occurred between the runtime and your network (ELB/socket layer) — likely packet loss or transient connection issues caused the token stream to be interrupted on your side.

Action items and recommendations
- We recommend running a mirrored test from your staging environment that preserves the same ELB/network path (or issuing the same request from an instance outside the ELB to rule it out).
- If you can reproduce, capture a full tcpdump from the client side and share it with our network team (network@redwoodinference.com). We’ll correlate PCAPs with server-side traces.
- SDK note: older SDK versions can interact poorly with certain ELB idle/keepalive configurations. If you prefer, upgrade to SDK v1.6.0 which includes more robust streaming keepalive handling.

We’re marking this as closed on the Redwood side for now since there’s no platform evidence of a service stall. If you continue to see occurrences after trying the steps above, please re-open ticket SP-8342 and share a reproduction. We’re happy to run a live debug session.

Best —
